_meta.indication: Prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season, and in children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; infants randomized 2:1 to a single 50 mg IM dose of nirsevimab or placebo prior to their first RSV season.
pivotal_trials.population: Otherwise healthy preterm neonates and infants born at ≥29 to <35 weeks gestational age, enrolled prior to their first RSV season.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Incidence of medically-attended (MA) RSV LRTI over the 5-month RSV season.
pivotal_trials.result: MA RSV LRTI 2.6% (25/969) nirsevimab vs 9.5% (46/484) placebo; relative risk reduction 70.1% (95% CI 52.3% to 81.2%), p<0.0001. Secondary endpoint RSV hospitalization 0.8% (8/969) vs 4.1% (20/484); RRR 78.4% (95% CI 51.9%, 90.3%), p=0.0002.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; infants randomized 2:1 to a single weight-based IM dose of nirsevimab or placebo, divided into a Primary Cohort (efficacy analysis) and a Safety Cohort.
pivotal_trials.population: Otherwise healthy preterm and term infants born at ≥35 weeks gestational age, enrolled prior to their first RSV season.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Incidence of medically-attended (MA) RSV LRTI due to RT-PCR-confirmed RSV over the 5-month RSV season (Primary Cohort).
pivotal_trials.result: MA RSV LRTI 1.2% (12/994) nirsevimab vs 5.0% (25/496) placebo; relative risk reduction 74.9% (95% CI 50.6% to 87.3%), p<0.0001. Secondary endpoint RSV hospitalization 0.6% (6/994) vs 1.6% (8/496); RRR 60.2% (95% CI -14.6%, 86.2%), p=0.09.

key_safety: Favorable safety profile. Most common adverse reactions in the pooled Trials 03 and 04 safety population (N=2,570 nirsevimab vs N=1,284 placebo) were rash (0.9% vs 0.6%) and injection site reactions (0.3% vs 0%). Key safety concerns are hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and serious skin reactions (not reported in clinical trials).
target_moa: Nirsevimab is a recombinant human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody that binds the prefusion conformation of the RSV fusion (F) protein at antigenic site Ø, neutralizing the virus; its Fc region carries the YTE (M252Y/S254T/T256E) substitutions to extend serum half-life for season-long protection.

advisory_committee.vote: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (June 8, 2023) unanimously voted that the overall benefit-risk assessment favors nirsevimab for the first RSV season indication; a majority (19/21) agreed the assessment was favorable for the second RSV season indication.

summary.text: BLA 761328 for nirsevimab-alip was submitted by AstraZeneca AB and received a standard review. The product had Fast Track designation (granted January 26, 2015) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (granted February 1, 2019). The application was presented at an Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on June 8, 2023 and was approved (traditional approval based on two placebo-controlled efficacy trials, not accelerated approval).
